obligations.note: routes.py adds POST /payees/{id}/reopen with the privileged action manage_payees and mfa=False, so a privileged route does not require MFA. The registered exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails on exactly this route, and EXC-0258 does not cover it (see EXC-1).

EXC-0258 is approved by a risk_owner, is unexpired and names a compensating control. But it is scoped to component payments.http, while the deviating mfa=False entry is in routes.py, which is component payments.routes. Its stated scope is also the reconciliation batch account, yet the code lets any role holding manage_payees use the route without MFA.

Ledger entry ACR-0404 supports MFA-1 and covers routes.py, which this change alters in behaviour, so that entry lapses. The only new evidence of the same strength is the exhaustive route control test, and it fails.

run.json reports result 'failure', and the JUnit report shows the registered MFA-1 control test failing. The report's provenance is also doubtful: its timestamp is 2026-10-23, before the head commit of 2026-10-27, and its host is a personal Mac rather than ci-runner-09.

Ticket CHG-26710 was approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-27T07:37Z, before the reviews. Its components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, payments.store) cover all four touched files.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa, a change_approver for payments and a different person from the author, sofia.santos.
Both approvals name head commit 30fdc36, which is the only commit in the change.
The change touches security-sensitive components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.store). Security reviewer ines.halvorsen gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
The new reopen_payee in service.py calls _audit, which records actor, action 'reopen_payee', target payee:{id} and the clock time, matching the existing pattern.

Inspecting the full store.py at head, the new execute call uses a fixed literal UPDATE statement with the id bound as a ? parameter, and every other call site uses fixed constants. The CI report's provenance is questionable, so this rests on inspection.
The new Store.reopen_payee only updates status and closed_at and writes no NPI column, so the sealing path is unaffected.

Reopening clears closed_at without checking that the payee is closed or that its NPI has been purged, so a close/reopen cycle could reset the retention clock. No retention-specific evidence for this new path is provided, and the CI report is of doubtful provenance.

summary: The change adds a privileged payee-reopen route (manage_payees) without MFA. The cited exception EXC-0258 is scoped to payments.http, not to the route-table component payments.routes, and the code does not restrict the route to the batch account the exception describes. The change's own CI run failed on the exhaustive MFA-1 control test, and its JUnit report appears to predate the head commit and come from a local machine. MFA-1, EXC-1, LAP-1 and CHG-4 are refuted, so the change is rejected.
